domain_label: Instructional Media & 3D Flashcard Producer — Image → Tripo → GLB → In-Browser 3D Card Pipeline
purpose: A method for turning a source image (or a small front/back/left/right capture set) into a web-renderable 3D anatomy flashcard: gating 3D on whether it actually aids spatial learning versus being decoration, driving Tripo's image_to_model / multiview_to_model async tasks, taking GLB output through optional conversion to GLTF/USDZ/FBX/OBJ/STL/3MF, and rendering a rotatable card in-browser with <model-viewer> or three.js — kept honest by tracing every vendor claim to EXTERNAL_RECON §7, tagging pedagogy claims as ESTIMATE-to-source-verify, and refusing to invent Tripo pricing or endpoints.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base scores are heuristic priors and every pedagogy call (3D-helps-vs-decoration, capture ergonomics) is an ESTIMATE synthesized from multimedia-learning and anatomy-education literature not source-verified in this build

all Tripo and model-viewer capabilities are transcribed from EXTERNAL_RECON §7 (itself grounded in the official tripo3d Python SDK and google/model-viewer), and Tripo pricing/credit costs are held UNKNOWN because the billing page was egress-blocked

source images are produced upstream by Codex MCP through the extint specialist; this KB consumes images and does not own image generation, and image-occlusion 2D card production is a neighboring media-KB slice this KB only references
the app is a single-user Base44 web app whose backend calls Tripo from a serverless function with a user-supplied TRIPO_API_KEY stored as a per-app Secret
exclusions: the image-occlusion 2D card pipeline and diagram authoring (a neighboring media KB) beyond naming it as the 2D alternative the pedagogy gate weighs 3D against
the Codex-MCP image-generation call, its prompts, model choice and cost (owned by extint) beyond stating that clean single-subject images are the required input
the flashcard scheduling, question authoring and knowledge-graph placement of the resulting card (owned by sched/qcraft/contenteng) beyond emitting a finished 3D card asset
Base44 platform-ops, Secrets handling and serverless wiring (owned by extint) beyond noting the backend-function-with-stored-key call pattern
training or hosting any 3D reconstruction model in-house; Tripo is treated as the external image-to-3D service and its internal method is out of scope

competency_questions.question: What is the image-to-3D-flashcard pipeline, and where does the media producer's ownership begin and end relative to contenteng and extint?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the image -> Tripo -> GLB -> in-browser <model-viewer> card chain, that extint/Codex-MCP produces source images and contenteng consumes 2D images for occlusion while nobody else produces 3D media, and names the single-user Base44 backend-function call pattern

competency_questions.question: When does a 3D model actually help learning versus being decoration, and how is that gate applied before any asset is generated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ties 3D value to spatial/structural anatomy where rotation and depth carry the concept, contrasts it with flat/text-labeled content better served by 2D image-occlusion, and cites the multimedia-learning basis as ESTIMATE-to-source-verify

competency_questions.question: Where do the source images come from and what upstream boundary does the pipeline depend on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names Codex MCP via the extint specialist as the image generator, states this KB consumes rather than produces images, and notes the single-clean-subject requirement handed downstream

competency_questions.question: What must a source image look like for Tripo to reconstruct a usable mesh?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: requires a single centered subject, clean/separable background, even lighting and no watermark or collage, and explains that violations drive hallucinated or warped geometry

competency_questions.question: What is Tripo's task-based async flow and how is it authenticated and called from the app?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gives the create-task -> poll/wait -> download-outputs cycle, the TRIPO_API_KEY auth and get_balance() credit check, and the backend-function-with-Secret call pattern, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

competency_questions.question: What does image_to_model do with one image and which mesh/texture parameters control the result?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states image_to_model takes one reference image and lists model_version, texture, pbr, texture_quality (standard|detailed), face_limit, quad and smart_low_poly as the levers, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

competency_questions.question: How does multiview_to_model use multiple images, how many are required, and what capture flow feeds it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states front is REQUIRED with back/left/right optional (2-4 images total), that consistent scale/lighting across views matters, and describes the front/back/left/right capture-then-reconstruct flow, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

competency_questions.question: How do you decide between single-image and multiview reconstruction for a given card?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: trades single-image speed/one-image-cost against multiview's better back and occluded geometry, and picks multiview when unseen surfaces carry learning value and single when the subject is near-symmetric or front-only

competency_questions.question: What is Tripo's native output format and which conversions are available for other targets?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states task output is GLB (model.glb, base_model, pbr_model) and convert_model supports GLTF/USDZ/FBX/OBJ/STL/3MF with quad/face_limit/texture_size options, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

competency_questions.question: Why is USDZ the Vision Pro forward path and when should conversion to it happen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: identifies USDZ as the Apple AR/Vision Pro consumable produced by convert_model, frames it as a forward path not a present requirement, and says convert on demand rather than pre-forking every asset

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states <model-viewer> renders glTF/GLB with one HTML tag (three.js-based loader, DRACO/KTX2 supported) and that three.js GLTFLoader is the general-purpose alternative when custom interaction is needed, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

competency_questions.question: How is a 3D card kept performant in a browser, especially on mobile?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: sets a face_limit and texture_size budget and uses DRACO mesh + KTX2 texture compression to keep GLB small enough to load and rotate without jank on a mobile device

competency_questions.question: What turns a rendered model into a usable rotatable study card?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: describes camera-controls/auto-rotate interaction, a stable framing and a study prompt so the learner manipulates the structure, and ties the interaction back to the spatial-learning rationale

competency_questions.question: What is the end-to-end pipeline verdict, how is the mesh quality-checked, and what remains cost-UNKNOWN?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: records the go pipeline (pedagogy-gate -> clean image -> single/multiview Tripo task -> GLB -> QC -> web-optimize -> model-viewer rotatable card, USDZ deferred), the mesh QC gate that blocks bad meshes, asset storage/serving, and that Tripo pricing is UNKNOWN and must be fetched before batch runs

glossary.definition: Tripo SDK call that reconstructs a single 3D mesh from ONE reference image; parameters include model_version, texture, pbr, texture_quality (standard|detailed), texture_alignment, face_limit, quad and smart_low_poly [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Fast and one-image-cheap but must infer all unseen (back/side) geometry, so it risks hallucinated surfaces.

Tripo SDK call that reconstructs one mesh from up to four views passed as [front, back, left, right] where FRONT is REQUIRED and back/left/right are optional, i.e. 2-4 images total [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Extra views constrain otherwise-hallucinated geometry at the cost of a multi-image capture step.

The web-native 3D asset format: glTF is the JSON+binary transmission format and GLB its single-file binary packaging. Tripo's task output is GLB (model.glb, base_model, pbr_model) [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7], and <model-viewer>/three.js render glTF/GLB directly, making GLB the canonical asset this pipeline stores.

Tripo conversion call taking a generated model to GLTF, USDZ, FBX, OBJ, STL or 3MF, with quad, face_limit and texture_size/format options [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Used on demand for targets other than web GLB — notably USDZ for Apple AR/Vision Pro.

Apple's AR-oriented single-file 3D format consumable by AR Quick Look and the Vision Pro visionOS stack; produced here via Tripo convert_model(format='USDZ') [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for the conversion support]. Treated as a forward path — converted on demand when the Vision Pro experience is actually built, not pre-generated for every card.

Google's web component that renders a glTF/GLB in-browser from a single HTML tag using a three.js-based loader with DRACO and KTX2 support and built-in camera-controls/auto-rotate [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 citing google/model-viewer]. The default renderer for a rotatable 3D flashcard; three.js GLTFLoader is the lower-level alternative.

DRACO is a geometry (mesh) compression codec and KTX2 (Basis Universal) a GPU texture compression container; both are supported by the <model-viewer>/three.js loaders [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. They shrink a GLB's download and GPU footprint so a card loads and rotates smoothly on a mobile browser.

The cap on triangle/quad count (a Tripo image_to_model / convert_model parameter) that bounds mesh complexity [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]; the web-performance budget sets it low enough that the GLB renders without jank on a target device, trading fine surface detail for interactivity.

The decision, made BEFORE generation, of whether a rotatable 3D model materially aids learning a concept — true for spatial/structural anatomy whose shape and depth are the content, false for flat or text-labeled material better taught by a 2D image-occlusion card [ESTIMATE — grounded in multimedia-learning and anatomy-education research, to source-verify]. It prevents spending Tripo credits and load budget on decoration.

The upstream input: a generated reference image produced by Codex MCP through the extint specialist, consumed (not produced) by this pipeline. Its quality — a single centered subject on a clean background — determines reconstruction quality, so image acceptance is this KB's first checkpoint.

nodes.definition: Frame the whole job: turn a source image (or a small multi-view set) into a web-renderable, rotatable 3D flashcard through the chain image -> Tripo (image_to_model | multiview_to_model) -> GLB -> in-browser <model-viewer>/three.js card [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for the tool chain]. Fix ownership boundaries: extint's Codex MCP PRODUCES the source images and contenteng CONSUMES 2D images for occlusion cards, while producing 3D media is this specialist's slice that nobody else owns [FACT-source: SPECIALIST_LIST §C4]. The runtime is a single-user Base44 web app calling Tripo from a serverless backend function with a user-supplied TRIPO_API_KEY stored as a per-app Secret [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6-7]. 3D is applied selectively, gated on pedagogy, not by default.

included: the image -> Tripo -> GLB -> in-browser card chain
the produce-3D-media ownership boundary vs extint (image gen) and contenteng (2D occlusion)
the single-user Base44 backend-function call pattern

pros.claim: Naming the full chain and the ownership boundaries stops the 3D producer from duplicating image generation or occlusion work and clarifies its single deliverable
pros.example: handing a finished rotatable GLB card downstream while leaving image synthesis to extint and 2D occlusion to contenteng

cons.claim: A multi-service chain (Codex MCP -> Tripo -> Base44 render) has several external failure points the frame must keep visible
cons.example: a card that fails because the upstream image was poor, not because Tripo or the renderer erred

failure_modes: treating 3D as the default medium instead of a pedagogy-gated option
blurring the boundary and re-implementing image generation or occlusion here
acceptance_tests: the frame states the image->Tripo->GLB->model-viewer chain, the produce-3D ownership boundary vs extint and contenteng, and the single-user Base44 backend-function pattern with citations
revisit_triggers: the specialist boundary in SPECIALIST_LIST changes
the app moves off Base44 or beyond a single user
a new 3D source service replaces Tripo

base.update_signal: a boundary change or a platform/vendor swap revises the frame

nodes.definition: Apply the pedagogy gate BEFORE generating any asset: a rotatable 3D model earns its cost only when spatial structure — shape, depth, the relationship of surfaces you must turn to see — IS the concept, as in the 3D form of a tooth, skull foramina, or vessel branching [ESTIMATE — grounded in multimedia-learning theory (a graphic must carry essential, not extraneous, information) and anatomy-education evidence that 3D aids spatial tasks; to source-verify in an L1 research pass]. When content is flat, symbolic, or text-labeled, a 2D image-occlusion card teaches it as well or better and 3D becomes decoration that spends credits, load budget and attention for no learning gain. The gate outputs a yes/no per concept and is the first filter of the pipeline; a no routes the concept to the 2D occlusion slice instead.

included: the decoration failure when 3D adds no learning

pros.claim: Gating on pedagogy prevents wasting Tripo credits and browser load budget on 3D that does not teach
pros.example: declining a 3D model of a labeled 2D pathway diagram and making an occlusion card instead

cons.claim: The 3D-helps criterion rests on general multimedia-learning claims not source-verified here, so borderline concepts are judgment calls
cons.example: an ambiguous surface-anatomy topic where 3D might or might not beat an annotated photo

failure_modes: defaulting to 3D for visual appeal and drowning the concept in extraneous detail
denying 3D for a genuinely spatial structure that rotation would clarify
acceptance_tests: the gate states the spatial-structure-is-the-content criterion, the decoration anti-pattern, and the route-to-2D-occlusion outcome, with the pedagogy basis tagged ESTIMATE-to-source-verify
revisit_triggers: learning data shows 3D not improving retention on a concept type
the multimedia-learning basis is source-verified and revises the criterion
the 2D occlusion slice changes what it can cover

base.update_signal: retention data or a source-verified pedagogy basis changes the gate

nodes.definition: Fix where the input image comes from: Codex MCP, called through the extint specialist, is the image generator; this pipeline CONSUMES a reference image and does not own its synthesis [FACT-source: SPECIALIST_LIST §C4 — 'Codex MCP (via extint) is the image generator']. The producer's job is to specify what a good input is (single centered subject, clean background) and to reject inputs that will not reconstruct, handing the generation prompt/retry back to extint rather than building an image pipeline here. Real anatomical photographs or licensed atlas imagery are the alternative input when a generated image would misrepresent clinical truth, a boundary handled with the content specialists.

included: specifying good-input requirements back to the generator
excluded: the Codex MCP call, prompts and cost (extint)
clinical-truth certification of the image content

pros.claim: Delegating image synthesis to extint keeps this pipeline focused on reconstruction and rendering, not prompt engineering
pros.example: requesting a regenerated cleaner front image from extint instead of post-processing a bad one here

cons.claim: Depending on an upstream generator means input quality and clinical accuracy are only partly controllable here
cons.example: a generated tooth image that is anatomically plausible but subtly wrong, needing a content-specialist check

failure_modes: rebuilding image generation inside this pipeline
accepting an anatomically inaccurate generated image without a content check
acceptance_tests: the node names Codex MCP via extint as the generator, states the consume-not-produce boundary, and specifies the good-input requirements passed back upstream
revisit_triggers: extint changes the image-generation interface
clinical-accuracy failures recur on generated images
a licensed-atlas image source is added

base.update_signal: an extint interface change or recurring accuracy failures change the source contract

nodes.definition: Define what a source image must be for Tripo to reconstruct a usable mesh: a single centered subject, a clean and separable (ideally plain) background, even lighting without harsh shadows or specular blowout, and no watermark, caption or collage of multiple objects [ESTIMATE — standard single-image photogrammetry/image-to-3D input practice; the specific Tripo tolerances are UNKNOWN and to be measured]. Violations propagate: a busy background gets fused into the mesh, a watermark becomes surface texture, multiple subjects confuse the reconstruction, and uneven lighting bakes false relief into the geometry. Input acceptance is the first checkpoint, cheaper to fix (regenerate the image) than a bad mesh (rerun a whole Tripo task).

included: how each violation corrupts the mesh
input acceptance as the cheapest checkpoint

pros.claim: Rejecting a bad input before spending a Tripo task is far cheaper than QC-failing the resulting mesh
pros.example: sending back a collage image for regeneration rather than reconstructing a fused two-object blob

cons.claim: The requirements are heuristic and the true Tripo tolerances are unmeasured, so some accepted images still reconstruct poorly
cons.example: a subtly uneven-lit image that passes the checklist but bakes a false ridge into the mesh

failure_modes: reconstructing from a multi-subject or watermarked image
baking background or lighting artifacts into the geometry
acceptance_tests: the node lists the single-subject/clean-background/even-lighting/no-watermark requirements, explains how violations corrupt the mesh, and marks the exact tolerances UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: measured Tripo input tolerances become available
a class of accepted images keeps reconstructing poorly
a new Tripo model version changes input robustness

base.update_signal: measured tolerances or a robustness change updates the input checklist

nodes.definition: Drive Tripo through its task-based ASYNC flow: create a task, poll or wait for completion, then download the outputs; authentication is an API key (TRIPO_API_KEY env or constructor) and get_balance() returns the remaining credit balance [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7, from the official tripo3d Python SDK]. In the single-user Base44 app the call runs from a serverless backend function with the key stored as a per-app Secret, never from the browser [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §6]. Because tasks are asynchronous, the app must handle pending/timeout states and not block a request thread; because credits are consumed per task and pricing is UNKNOWN, a balance check precedes any batch.

included: TRIPO_API_KEY auth and get_balance() credit check

pros.claim: Modeling the async task lifecycle explicitly keeps the app responsive and prevents blocking on a slow reconstruction
pros.example: creating a task, returning a pending card state, and finishing when the poll reports done

cons.claim: Async plus opaque per-task cost means the app must manage pending/timeout/credit states it cannot fully predict
cons.example: a task that stays pending far longer than a typical run with no cost estimate to bound retries

failure_modes: blocking a request thread waiting synchronously for a task
calling Tripo from the browser and exposing the API key
acceptance_tests: the node gives the create/poll/download async cycle, the TRIPO_API_KEY auth and get_balance() check, and the backend-function-with-Secret non-blocking pattern, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7
revisit_triggers: Tripo changes its task API or SDK
task timeouts become common
credit-exhaustion incidents occur

base.update_signal: a task-API change or credit-exhaustion incidents change the flow

nodes.definition: Use image_to_model(image=...) to reconstruct a mesh from ONE reference image [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. It is the fastest, one-image-cheap path and works when a single front view is enough, but by definition it must INFER all unseen geometry (back and occluded sides), so those surfaces are hallucinated and may be wrong. The SDK default model_version in the recon is 'v2.5-20250123' with newer versions (v3.x/Turbo) announced but unconfirmed [SIGNAL, verify]. This node is the single-view branch of the reconstruction step; its output feeds GLB download and mesh QC, and its inferred-back-geometry weakness is exactly what pushes symmetric or view-critical subjects toward multiview.

excluded: the mesh/texture parameter list (its own node)

pros.claim: One image and one task produce a full mesh fast and cheap when only the front view matters
pros.example: reconstructing a near-symmetric molar crown from a single clean occlusal image

cons.claim: All unseen surfaces are inferred, so back and side geometry can be confidently wrong
cons.example: a plausible but fabricated root morphology on a tooth reconstructed from one crown photo

failure_modes: trusting inferred back/side geometry as accurate
using single-image where the unseen surfaces carry the learning value
acceptance_tests: the node states image_to_model reconstructs from one image, notes the speed/cost benefit and the hallucinated-unseen-geometry limit, and cites EXTERNAL_RECON §7 with the model_version SIGNAL
revisit_triggers: a new Tripo model version improves single-image back inference
single-image QC fail rate stays high
the default model_version is confirmed

base.update_signal: a model-version improvement or a high single-image fail rate changes the branch use

nodes.definition: Use multiview_to_model(images=[front, back, left, right]) to reconstruct from up to FOUR views where FRONT is REQUIRED and back/left/right are optional, i.e. 2-4 images total [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Extra views constrain the geometry the single-image path would hallucinate, giving far more trustworthy back and side surfaces — the difference between a study-accurate model and a decorative front shell. The cost is a real capture step: the views must be of the same subject at consistent scale, orientation and lighting, or the reconstruction warps. This is the multi-view branch; it is the default when unseen surfaces carry learning value.

included: the [front,back,left,right] 2-4 image call with front REQUIRED
excluded: the capture ergonomics workflow (its own node)

pros.claim: Adding views constrains otherwise-hallucinated geometry, yielding study-accurate back and side surfaces
pros.example: a four-view skull fragment whose foramina are correctly placed rather than invented

cons.claim: It needs a coordinated multi-image capture at consistent scale and lighting, which is more work and can warp if inconsistent
cons.example: front and back images at different distances producing a lopsided mesh

failure_modes: mixing inconsistent-scale or inconsistent-lighting views and warping the mesh
omitting the required front view
acceptance_tests: the node states front is REQUIRED with back/left/right optional (2-4 images), the improved-unseen-geometry benefit, and the consistent-capture requirement, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7
revisit_triggers: Tripo changes the view count or requirements
warped multiview meshes recur
capture ergonomics change

base.update_signal: a view-requirement change or recurring warps change the multiview branch

nodes.definition: Specify the capture flow that feeds multiview: acquire front (required) and as many of back/left/right as the subject needs, keeping the subject at a consistent distance, orientation baseline and lighting across shots so the views register into one coherent mesh [ESTIMATE — multi-view capture practice; the exact tolerances Tripo accepts are UNKNOWN]. For generated imagery this means prompting extint for a consistent multi-angle SET of the same subject rather than four unrelated images; for real objects it means a turntable-style capture. The output is the ordered [front, back, left, right] list handed to multiview_to_model, and this is the 'multi-image capture -> 3D -> rotatable card' flow named in the specialist brief.

included: acquiring consistent front/back/left/right views of one subject

pros.claim: A disciplined consistent-angle capture set is what makes multiview's accuracy gain real rather than a warped average
pros.example: prompting one subject from four consistent angles so the views fuse cleanly

cons.claim: Getting a consistent same-subject multi-angle set (especially from a generator) is harder than one image and can silently drift
cons.example: four generated 'views' that are actually four slightly different teeth

failure_modes: assembling views of subtly different subjects
inconsistent scale/orientation across the capture set
acceptance_tests: the node describes acquiring consistent front/back/left/right views of one subject and the ordered hand-off to multiview_to_model, with tolerances marked UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: multiview meshes show cross-view drift
extint gains reliable multi-angle consistent generation
a turntable capture tool is added

base.update_signal: cross-view drift or better multi-angle generation changes the capture flow

nodes.definition: Set the mesh and texture knobs on the reconstruction: texture on/off, pbr (physically based material maps), texture_quality standard|detailed, texture_alignment, face_limit (triangle/quad cap), quad (quad vs triangulated topology) and smart_low_poly [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. These trade fidelity against weight: pbr + detailed textures + high face_limit give a rich model but a heavy GLB, while smart_low_poly + a capped face_limit give a light model that renders on a phone. The right setting is dictated downstream by the web-performance budget and upstream by the pedagogy gate — enough detail to carry the structure, no more. Parameters are chosen BEFORE generation because changing them means rerunning the task.

excluded: the web-performance budget that constrains them (its own node)

pros.claim: Explicit parameters let one generation target the right fidelity-weight point instead of regenerating to fix it
pros.example: setting smart_low_poly and a face_limit up front for a mobile-first card

cons.claim: Over-set fidelity (pbr + detailed + high face_limit) produces a heavy GLB that janks on-device
cons.example: a detailed-texture high-poly model that stutters when rotated on a phone

failure_modes: maxing fidelity and shipping a GLB too heavy for the browser
changing parameters after generation and paying for a rerun
acceptance_tests: the node lists texture/pbr/texture_quality/face_limit/quad/smart_low_poly, explains the fidelity-vs-weight trade, and states parameters are chosen pre-generation, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7
revisit_triggers: the web-performance budget changes
a new Tripo version adds or renames parameters
on-device jank recurs

base.update_signal: a budget change or parameter-set change updates the knobs

nodes.definition: Carry Tripo pricing as an explicit UNKNOWN: exact per-task credit costs are not verifiable in this build (the billing page was egress-blocked) and must NOT be invented [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 marks pricing UNKNOWN with a METHOD]. The [METHOD] to obtain them is to read https://platform.tripo3d.ai/docs/billing or the account dashboard, and until then get_balance() is the only ground truth. Operationally the app gates any batch on a balance check and treats a single high-value 3D card as more defensible than bulk generation whose cost cannot be estimated, so cost opacity biases the pipeline toward selective, pedagogy-gated generation rather than mass production.

included: Tripo per-task cost as a named UNKNOWN with its METHOD
get_balance() as the only current cost signal
cost opacity biasing toward selective generation

pros.claim: Naming cost as UNKNOWN with a fetch METHOD prevents fabricated pricing from driving a batch decision
pros.example: gating a bulk run on get_balance() rather than a guessed per-model price

cons.claim: Without real prices, batch planning and budgeting are blind and rely on balance draw-down as a lagging signal
cons.example: discovering a run was expensive only after the balance drops

failure_modes: inventing a per-task price to plan a batch
running bulk generation without a balance check
acceptance_tests: the node marks Tripo pricing UNKNOWN with the billing-page/dashboard METHOD, names get_balance() as the only cost signal, and states the bias toward selective generation, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7
revisit_triggers: Tripo pricing is fetched and confirmed
a batch unexpectedly drains the balance
a credit-alert threshold is added

base.update_signal: fetched pricing or a balance-drain incident changes the cost handling

nodes.definition: Take the task output as GLB — the download yields model.glb with base_model and pbr_model components [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. GLB (the single-file binary packaging of glTF) is the web-native format that <model-viewer> and three.js render directly, so it is the CANONICAL asset the pipeline stores and serves; every other format is a derived conversion. Downloading the GLB is the hand-off from generation to rendering: it is what mesh QC inspects, what the web-performance step compresses, and what the rotatable card embeds. Keeping GLB canonical and converting only on demand avoids forking the asset into stale format copies.

included: GLB as the native task output (model.glb, base_model, pbr_model)
GLB as the web-native canonical stored asset
excluded: the conversions to other formats (its own node)

pros.claim: Treating GLB as the single canonical asset keeps one source of truth that renders natively on the web
pros.example: storing model.glb once and rendering it directly in <model-viewer> without conversion

cons.claim: GLB alone does not serve non-web targets, so AR/DCC needs on-demand conversion that must be kept in sync
cons.example: needing a separate USDZ for Vision Pro that can go stale if the GLB is re-generated

failure_modes: forking into many format copies that drift from the GLB
losing the pbr_model/base_model distinction when storing
acceptance_tests: the node states the GLB task output (model.glb, base_model, pbr_model), names GLB the web-native canonical asset, and frames download as the render hand-off, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7
revisit_triggers: Tripo changes its output packaging
a non-web target becomes primary
asset-sync drift appears across formats

base.update_signal: an output-format change or sync drift changes the canonical-asset handling

nodes.definition: Convert the GLB on demand with convert_model(format=...), which supports GLTF, USDZ, FBX, OBJ, STL and 3MF plus quad, face_limit and texture_size/format options [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Each target has a purpose: GLTF/GLB for web, USDZ for Apple AR/Vision Pro, FBX/OBJ for DCC and engine import, STL/3MF for 3D printing. Conversion is a SEPARATE task keyed off the canonical GLB, done only when a target actually needs it — pre-converting every asset to every format wastes credits and creates stale copies. This node is the branch point to USDZ (the Vision Pro path) and any print/engine export.

included: convert_model support for GLTF/USDZ/FBX/OBJ/STL/3MF and quad/face_limit/texture_size
excluded: the USDZ/Vision Pro decision (its own node)

pros.claim: On-demand conversion from the canonical GLB reaches AR, DCC and print targets without maintaining parallel pipelines
pros.example: producing an STL for a 3D print only when a physical model is requested

cons.claim: Every conversion is another task and another artifact to keep consistent with the GLB
cons.example: a USDZ generated before a GLB re-run, leaving the AR copy stale

failure_modes: pre-converting to every format speculatively
letting a converted artifact drift from the updated GLB

nodes.definition: Treat USDZ as the Apple AR / Vision Pro FORWARD path: convert_model(format='USDZ') yields the format AR Quick Look and the visionOS stack consume [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for the conversion support; the Vision Pro consumption of USDZ is Apple-platform general knowledge, ESTIMATE-to-source-verify]. It is a forward path, not a present requirement — the web <model-viewer> card is the shipping experience now, and USDZ is generated on demand when a spatial/Vision Pro experience is actually built. Pre-converting every card to USDZ spends credits on an unbuilt feature and risks stale AR copies. The node marks the seam where this pipeline could extend from a rotatable web card to a headset-native model.

nodes.definition: Render the GLB in-browser with Google's <model-viewer> web component: one HTML tag loads and displays a glTF/GLB using a three.js-based loader with DRACO and KTX2 support and built-in camera-controls/auto-rotate [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 citing google/model-viewer]. It is the default renderer for a 3D flashcard because it turns 'display a rotatable model' into a declarative element with accessibility, poster, and AR-launch attributes handled. The producer's job is to point src at the stored GLB, set framing/lighting attributes, and confirm it loads under the app's content-security policy. three.js is the fallback when interaction beyond what the component exposes is needed.

nodes.definition: Keep three.js with GLTFLoader as the general-purpose rendering alternative to <model-viewer> [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. Because <model-viewer> is itself three.js-based, dropping to raw three.js buys full control — custom camera rigs, annotation hotspots pinned to mesh coordinates, cross-section clipping planes, synchronized multi-model scenes — at the cost of writing and maintaining the render loop, loaders and controls yourself. The decision rule: use <model-viewer> for a plain rotatable card (the common case) and reach for three.js only when a study interaction (labeled pins, cutaways, quiz-driven highlighting) exceeds what the component exposes. Both consume the same canonical GLB.

nodes.definition: Shrink the GLB with DRACO geometry compression and KTX2 (Basis Universal) GPU-texture compression, both supported by the <model-viewer>/three.js loaders [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7]. DRACO cuts the mesh's byte size for faster download and KTX2 stores textures in a GPU-native compressed form that lowers both download and VRAM use, together making the difference between a card that streams in and one that stalls. Compression complements the pre-generation face_limit/texture budget: parameters cap what is generated, DRACO/KTX2 cap what is transmitted. The trade is a small decode cost and possible minor quality loss, acceptable for a study card where interactivity beats pixel-perfection.

included: DRACO mesh and KTX2 texture compression supported by the loaders
compression as complement to the generation budget

pros.claim: DRACO+KTX2 cut download and GPU memory enough to make a heavy model usable on mobile
pros.example: a compressed GLB that streams in on a phone where the raw file stalled

cons.claim: Compression adds a decode step and can slightly degrade mesh/texture quality
cons.example: faint texture banding from aggressive KTX2 on a fine surface

failure_modes: shipping an uncompressed heavy GLB to the browser
over-compressing and visibly degrading the study surface
acceptance_tests: the node names DRACO mesh and KTX2 texture compression as loader-supported, explains their download/VRAM benefit, and frames them as complementary to the generation budget, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

base.update_signal: a load-time regression or a support change updates the compression step

nodes.definition: Set a web-performance budget that bounds the delivered card: a face_limit (poly count) and texture_size ceiling chosen so the GLB downloads quickly and rotates at a smooth frame rate on a target MOBILE browser, since a study card is often used on a phone [ESTIMATE — general web-3D performance practice; concrete poly/byte thresholds are device-dependent and to be measured on the app's target devices]. The budget feeds back into the Tripo mesh/texture parameters (cap generation) and forward into DRACO/KTX2 (cap transmission), and is a hard constraint on the pipeline verdict: a model that cannot render smoothly on-device is not shippable no matter how accurate. Interactivity is weighted above fine detail because a janky card teaches nothing.

included: a face_limit and texture_size budget for smooth mobile rendering
its feedback into generation params and compression
excluded: the exact device-measured thresholds (to be measured)

pros.claim: A performance budget makes on-device smoothness a first-class constraint instead of a post-hoc surprise
pros.example: capping face_limit so a card rotates fluidly on a mid-range phone

cons.claim: The thresholds are device-dependent and unmeasured here, so the budget is provisional until tested on real target devices
cons.example: a budget tuned for a desktop that still janks on an older phone

failure_modes: shipping a model that exceeds device budget and janks or crashes the tab

nodes.definition: Turn the rendered model into a usable STUDY card: enable camera-controls (drag to rotate, pinch to zoom) with a sensible auto-rotate and a stable default framing, pair it with the card's prompt/answer so the learner actively manipulates the structure, and set a poster/loading state so the card is legible before the GLB streams in [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for the <model-viewer> interaction attributes; the study-card pairing is design synthesis]. The point is active manipulation: rotating to find a landmark is the retrieval act the spatial-learning rationale predicted would help, closing the loop back to the pedagogy gate. A 3D card that cannot be rotated, or that spins decoratively without a study task, has lost its reason to be 3D.

tying the manipulation back to the spatial-learning rationale
excluded: the scheduling/answer-grading of the card (other specialists)

nodes.definition: Decide between the single-image and multiview branches per card by weighing accuracy against effort/cost. Choose single image when the subject is near-symmetric or the front view carries the concept and the unseen surfaces are not load-bearing (fastest, one image). Choose multiview when back/side/occluded geometry is exactly what the learner must study, since single-image inference will confidently fabricate it [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for both capabilities; the decision rule is design synthesis]. The tie-breaker is the pedagogy gate: if 3D was justified BECAUSE spatial all-around structure is the content, that same reason usually mandates multiview. Cost opacity biases toward not over-capturing, but accuracy on study-critical surfaces wins over saving one or two images.

included: the single-vs-multiview trade of accuracy against effort/cost
excluded: the reconstruction mechanics of each branch

pros.claim: An explicit rule stops both over-capturing symmetric subjects and under-capturing all-around structures
pros.example: single image for a symmetric crown, four views for a skull whose posterior surface is the lesson

cons.claim: The right call depends on judging which surfaces are study-critical, which is not always obvious pre-generation
cons.example: a subject whose back matters more than expected, discovered only after a single-image QC fail

failure_modes: single-image on a subject whose unseen geometry is the lesson

acceptance_tests: the node gives the single-vs-multiview accuracy-vs-effort trade, the study-critical-unseen-surface criterion, and the pedagogy-gate tie-breaker, cited to EXTERNAL_RECON §7

nodes.definition: Quality-control every generated mesh before it becomes a card: inspect for hallucinated or wrong geometry (especially unseen surfaces from single-image runs), fused background, warped topology from inconsistent multiview capture, missing PBR maps yielding a flat untextured look, and gross scale/orientation errors [ESTIMATE — standard generated-asset QC; the specific defect rates for Tripo are UNKNOWN and to be tracked]. A mesh that fails QC is not shipped: it is regenerated (better input, or switch single->multiview) rather than embedded, because a confidently wrong anatomy model mis-teaches worse than no model. QC is the gate between generation and rendering and the sensor whose fail patterns drive the single-vs-multiview default and the source-image checklist.

included: QC fail patterns feeding the branch default and input checklist
excluded: the clinical-accuracy certification of correct-looking geometry (content specialists)

pros.claim: A QC gate stops a confidently-wrong anatomy model from mis-teaching, which is worse than shipping no 3D
pros.example: rejecting a single-image tooth whose fabricated roots are anatomically impossible

cons.claim: QC is partly manual and cannot catch geometry that looks right but is clinically wrong, needing a content check
cons.example: a plausible mesh with a subtly misplaced landmark that passes visual QC

failure_modes: embedding a hallucinated or warped mesh as a study card

nodes.definition: Store and serve the canonical GLB (and any on-demand conversions) so the card can render: host the GLB as a static asset on the Base44 app's file storage/CDN, reference it by a stable URL from the <model-viewer> src, and cache it so repeated card views do not re-download [ESTIMATE — standard web-asset hosting on the Base44 platform; the exact storage/CDN limits are UNKNOWN and platform-owned by extint]. The concerns are a stable content-addressed path (so a regenerated model can version cleanly), CORS/CSP so the renderer may fetch it, and reasonable cache headers. This is the last mile between a QC-passed GLB and a rendered card, and it is where a mis-served or CSP-blocked asset shows up as a blank card.

CORS/CSP and cache-header concerns for the renderer

pros.claim: Stable content-addressed hosting with caching makes cards load fast and version cleanly on regeneration
pros.example: a regenerated model getting a new URL so cached old cards do not show stale geometry

cons.claim: Serving specifics (limits, CORS, CSP) are platform-owned and partly UNKNOWN here, so mis-serving surfaces as a blank card
cons.example: a CSP that blocks the GLB fetch leaving <model-viewer> empty

nodes.definition: Commit the end-to-end verdict for a 3D anatomy flashcard: gate on pedagogy (3D only where spatial structure is the content) -> accept a clean single-subject source image from extint/Codex MCP -> choose single vs multiview (multiview when unseen surfaces are study-critical) -> run the async Tripo task with a pre-set mesh/texture budget -> take the canonical GLB -> QC the mesh and block-and-regenerate on failure -> web-optimize with a face_limit budget plus DRACO/KTX2 -> embed a rotatable <model-viewer> card and serve the GLB from stable storage; USDZ/Vision Pro deferred as an on-demand forward path, three.js reserved for custom interaction [FACT-source: EXTERNAL_RECON §7 for every vendor capability; the assembly and gates are design synthesis]. The go conditions: pedagogy-justified, QC-passed, within the device performance budget, and a balance check because Tripo pricing is UNKNOWN — anything failing these is a no-go for that card.

excluded: the downstream scheduling of the finished card

pros.example: shipping one QC-passed, budget-fitting, pedagogy-justified skull card and declining a decorative one

cons.claim: The assembly rests on unmeasured pedagogy, cost and device thresholds, so the verdict is provisional until those are verified

workflow.gate: the card rotates with a retrieval prompt, loads under the app CSP, and serves from a stable versioned URL

workflow.description: Sign off only cards that are pedagogy-justified, QC-passed, within budget and balance-checked; defer USDZ/Vision Pro
workflow.gate: the verdict confirms the four go conditions and records USDZ deferred and three.js reserved, with vendor facts cited

dominance_rules.rule: The pedagogy gate dominates fidelity and visual appeal
dominance_rules.rationale: 3D that does not aid spatial learning is decoration that wastes credits, load budget and attention
dominance_rules.trigger: a 3D model is proposed for a concept
dominance_rules.action: generate 3D only where spatial structure is the content and route the rest to 2D image-occlusion

dominance_rules.rule: Multiview dominates single-image when unseen surfaces carry the concept
dominance_rules.rationale: single-image inference fabricates back/side geometry that a study-accurate model must not invent
dominance_rules.trigger: the subject's occluded surfaces are study-critical
dominance_rules.action: use multiview_to_model with a consistent front/back/left/right capture set

dominance_rules.rule: The device performance budget dominates texture and mesh fidelity
dominance_rules.rationale: a card that janks or crashes on a phone teaches nothing regardless of its detail
dominance_rules.trigger: generation parameters would exceed the mobile budget
dominance_rules.action: cap face_limit/texture_size and apply DRACO/KTX2 so interactivity is preserved

dominance_rules.rule: The QC gate dominates auto-publishing a generated mesh
dominance_rules.rationale: a confidently-wrong anatomy model mis-teaches worse than shipping no 3D
dominance_rules.trigger: a mesh is about to become a card
dominance_rules.action: run mesh QC and block-and-regenerate any hallucinated, warped or mis-scaled mesh

dominance_rules.rule: <model-viewer> dominates three.js for the common rotatable card
dominance_rules.rationale: the one-tag component delivers rotation, accessibility and AR launch with far less code to maintain
dominance_rules.trigger: a plain rotatable card is being built
dominance_rules.action: use <model-viewer> and reserve three.js for interactions it cannot express

dominance_rules.rule: Canonical GLB dominates premature multi-format export
dominance_rules.rationale: pre-converting to every format spends credits and creates stale copies
dominance_rules.action: keep the GLB canonical and convert (USDZ/OBJ/STL) only when a real target needs it

dominance_rules.rule: A balance check dominates bulk generation while pricing is UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.rationale: unbudgeted per-task cost can drain credits mid-batch with no estimate
dominance_rules.trigger: a batch generation is about to run
dominance_rules.action: call get_balance() first and bias toward few high-value pedagogy-gated cards

dominance_rules.rule: The present web card dominates the Vision Pro forward path
dominance_rules.rationale: USDZ/Vision Pro is a deferred option and pre-building AR spends on an unbuilt feature
dominance_rules.action: ship the web <model-viewer> card and keep USDZ a one-call on-demand conversion

dominance_rules.rule: Input rejection dominates reconstructing a bad image
dominance_rules.rationale: regenerating a clean image is far cheaper than a QC-failed Tripo task
dominance_rules.trigger: a source image fails the input checklist
dominance_rules.action: reject it and request a clean single-subject regeneration from extint before spending a task

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide 3D-vs-2D per concept before generating any asset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending a Tripo task and load budget on a model that should have been a 2D occlusion card

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the source image is a clean single subject before running a task
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a QC-failed reconstruction and a wasted task on a watermarked or multi-subject image

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose single vs multiview before capture
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recapturing a full multi-angle set after a single-image mesh fails on unseen surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the face_limit/texture budget before generation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating the model to fix a GLB too heavy for the browser

anti_rework_rules.rule: QC the mesh before embedding it in a card
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping and later retracting a hallucinated or warped model from a live card

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the GLB canonical and convert only on demand
anti_rework_rules.prevents: maintaining and re-syncing stale USDZ/OBJ/STL copies across regenerations

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm <model-viewer> and the GLB load under the app CSP/CORS before building many cards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a batch of blank cards from a CSP or serving block discovered late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the Tripo credit balance before a batch run
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a half-finished batch abandoned when credits run out mid-run at UNKNOWN cost

iteration_protocol.trigger: Tripo announces or confirms a new model version (v3.x/Turbo)
iteration_protocol.action: re-benchmark reconstruction quality and update the default model_version and single-image trust

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Vision Pro / AR experience is actually scoped
iteration_protocol.action: wire convert_model(format='USDZ') and AR Quick Look and source-verify the USDZ/visionOS requirements

iteration_protocol.trigger: single-image QC fail rate stays high on a subject type
iteration_protocol.action: switch that subject type's default to multiview and tighten the input checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: mobile jank or tab crashes are reported on 3D cards
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the face_limit/texture budget and apply or strengthen DRACO/KTX2 compression

iteration_protocol.trigger: Tripo pricing is fetched from the billing page or dashboard
iteration_protocol.action: add real cost gating to batch planning and relax the balance-only heuristic

iteration_protocol.trigger: the <model-viewer> component is blocked under the app CSP
iteration_protocol.action: move to a self-hosted three.js GLTFLoader render path

iteration_protocol.trigger: retention data shows 3D not improving learning on a concept type
iteration_protocol.action: revert that concept type to a 2D image-occlusion card and revise the pedagogy gate

priority_rationale: The pipeline frame and the pedagogy gate come first because they decide whether a 3D card should exist at all and where this specialist's ownership begins, keeping decoration and boundary-creep out before any credit is spent; the source-image provenance and quality checkpoint come next because reconstruction quality is capped by the input and rejecting a bad image is the cheapest fix; the Tripo async task flow, the single-image and multiview branches, the capture flow, the mesh/texture parameters and the cost-UNKNOWN gate then form the generation core; GLB output, format conversion and the deferred USDZ/Vision Pro path define the canonical asset and its on-demand derivatives; the model-viewer and three.js renderers, DRACO/KTX2 compression, the web-performance budget and the rotatable-card interaction turn the asset into a usable study object; and the single-vs-multiview decision, the mesh QC gate, asset storage/serving and the end-to-end verdict come last because they compose every upstream step into a gated, pedagogy-justified, QC-passed, budget-fitting, balance-checked deliverable with USDZ and three.js held as explicit forward options.
